subject: Re: Pricing anchor and stability guardrails — clarifying fee corridor
content:
From: Caroline Bates <caroline.bates@acmecloud.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Sellers <tom.sellers@acmecloud.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Pricing exhibits question — fee corridor and floor behaviour

Hi Grace,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. Legal ran the draft order form past procurement and they have a few follow-ups before we proceed to signature: in Exhibit C the ‘fee corridor’ language references both a monthly floor and an annual true-up. Procurement is worried about a scenario where heavy transient traffic in Q4 could push us over the cap and trigger an outsized true-up relative to the contracted month-by-month minima.

Two concrete asks:
- Can you confirm whether the monthly floor applies before or after the annual true-up calculation?
- Is there a stabilization clause to prevent a single month spike from re-setting the annual baseline?

They also asked that we see a redline that explicitly calls out the interaction (they want the math). I attached our internal summary of the concern (see attached: Exhibit C summary.pdf). Can your team propose clarifying language?

Appreciate the quick turn — we are trying to get onto counsel’s agenda this week.

Best,
Caroline
Caroline Bates
Director, Procurement
AcmeCloud

----
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Caroline Bates <caroline.bates@acmecloud.com>
Cc: Tom Sellers <tom.sellers@acmecloud.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 10:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Pricing exhibits question — fee corridor and floor behaviour

Caroline — thanks for the clear note. Quick answers up-front:
- The monthly floor is assessed on a per-month basis; the annual true-up reconciles the sum of monthly actuals vs committed annual minimums.
- We can add a stabilization carveout so that a single month spike above expected volume does not permanently raise the annual baseline used for indexing/true-up math.

I’ve asked Legal and Pricing to propose specific wording and a worked example (three lines of math) showing how a Q4 spike would be treated under both the current draft and the proposed stabilizer. See attached draft redline from our side (ACME_Orderform_Redline_v2.docx).

Proposed next steps:
1) Marissa and Karthik to align on acceptable stabilizer threshold (e.g., cap sustainment window of 3 months or a 50% spike smoothing rule).
2) We’ll provide a short illustrative table for counsel and re-upload the revised Exhibit C.

I’m keeping this on a tight timeline given your sign date.

Thanks,
Grace O'Connor
Head of Sales Operations, Redwood Inference
grace_oconnor@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

----
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Caroline Bates <caroline.bates@acmecloud.com>
Date: Wed, 2 Dec 2026 08:26:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Pricing exhibits question — fee corridor and floor behaviour

Folks — attaching a focused proposal. High level: we preserve the monthly floor and annual true-up mechanics but introduce a ‘stabilization window’ that prevents a one-month spike from permanently increasing the baseline used for the next annual true-up. Key points in the markup:
- Stabilization window defaults to 90 days unless otherwise negotiated.
- Spike smoothing uses a 3-month rolling average to compute the month’s contribution for baseline purposes when monthly actuals exceed the 90th percentile of prior 12 months.
- An exception bucket for acute product launches: customer may request a one-time carveout for verified launches; requires written notice.

Attachment: ACME_Orderform_Redline_v2.docx (contains inline tracked changes in Exhibit C). I also included a brief worked example showing how a 250% single-month spike in November would be amortized across Q4 and excluded from the baseline if not sustained.

Marissa
Marissa Cole
Sr. Contracts Manager, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com | +1 (650) 555-0198

Attachments: ACME_Orderform_Redline_v2.docx

From: Tom Sellers <tom.sellers@acmecloud.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Caroline Bates <caroline.bates@acmecloud.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 3 Dec 2026 11:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Pricing exhibits question — fee corridor and floor behaviour

Marissa — appreciate the fast turnaround. A few clarifying Qs from counsel:
- The 90-day stabilization window — does that mean the spike is ignored for baseline if it is followed by two months of drop-off, or is a three-month sustain required to count it in the baseline? Counsel wants the logic explicit.
- Can you add a worked formula in Exhibit C showing the exact arithmetic used for the three-month rolling average? They’ve asked for determinism (no ambiguous terms like ‘material decrease’ without thresholds).

Also, procurement flagged the one-time carveout flow: they want a notification timeline (e.g., written notice 10 business days before expected launch) and an audit right to verify launch traffic. Would you accept those constraints?

Thanks,
Tom Sellers
Legal Ops, AcmeCloud

----
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Tom Sellers <tom.sellers@acmecloud.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Caroline Bates <caroline.bates@acmecloud.com>
Date: Thu, 3 Dec 2026 16:42:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Pricing exhibits question — fee corridor and floor behaviour

Tom / Caroline — thanks for the feedback. Short answers:
- Stabilization: the intention is the spike is only reflected in the baseline if it is sustained for at least two of the following three months (i.e., a 2-out-of-3 sustain rule), which prevents a single-month outlier from raising future floors. I will add explicit wording to Exhibit C: "A month shall be included in baseline computation only if its normalized volume is at or above the spike threshold in at least two of the three-month rolling window."
- Formula: agree to include a deterministic formula and a worked numeric example (we will show the math using actual token counts and effective price).
- Carveout: 10 business days written notice + audit right is acceptable. We will add a clause requiring both notice and reasonable validation; validation scope limited to traffic metrics only (no access to PII).

I’ll update the markup now and send a final redline for your counsel to review. If that looks good, we can proceed to DocuSign and lock the deal.

Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Director, Pricing & Commercial Strategy
